listItemEnd.description: How list items end: no full stop, or a full stop.

quotes.description: Quotation marks and apostrophes: curly (“ ” ‘ ’) or straight (" ').

terms.description: Banned or replaced words and phrases.

checks.description: Headings use the house case ("headingCase": sentence, title or upper), keeping acronyms, words with digits and the profile's "properNouns".
Headings go no deeper than "maxHeadingLevel" (default 6) and never skip a level (a level 2 heading before any level 3).
List items end the house way ("listItemEnd": "none", no full stop, or "period", a full stop).
Quotation marks and apostrophes are curly (“ ” ‘ ’) or straight (" ') as "quotes" says. Code is left alone.
Words the house style avoids ("terms": { avoid, use?, note? }) do not appear, matched as whole words in any case. Code is left alone.
Numbers of five digits or more group thousands the house way ("thousandsSeparator": ",", ".", " ", "thin" or "none"). Four-digit numbers (years) and code are left alone.

allowNeutrals.description: Allow greys, black and white that are not in the palette. Default true.

<style_domain id="rich-text" file="rich-text.json">
Documents: How documents read: heading case and depth, list item endings, quotation marks, preferred terms, number and date formats, and the fonts and text colours allowed. Findings target ranges that replace_range accepts, with the replacement when the fix is certain.

Where it goes: rich-text.json in the skill folder, or under a "rich-text:" key in the SKILL.md frontmatter (not both). It applies when the skill's frontmatter "domains" includes rich-text, or names none.
A variant can build on another skill with "extends: <skill>" in its frontmatter and give only the fields that differ; objects merge field by field, lists and values replace.

Checks it can turn on in "checks" (an id, or { "id": ..., options }):
- heading-case: Headings use the house case ("headingCase": sentence, title or upper), keeping acronyms, words with digits and the profile's "properNouns".
- heading-levels: Headings go no deeper than "maxHeadingLevel" (default 6) and never skip a level (a level 2 heading before any level 3).
- list-punctuation: List items end the house way ("listItemEnd": "none", no full stop, or "period", a full stop).
- quotes: Quotation marks and apostrophes are curly (“ ” ‘ ’) or straight (" ') as "quotes" says. Code is left alone.
- terms: Words the house style avoids ("terms": { avoid, use?, note? }) do not appear, matched as whole words in any case. Code is left alone.
- number-format: Numbers of five digits or more group thousands the house way ("thousandsSeparator": ",", ".", " ", "thin" or "none"). Four-digit numbers (years) and code are left alone.
- date-format: Dates are written the house way ("dateFormat": "iso" 2026-11-12, "day-month-year" 12 November 2026, or "month-day-year" November 12, 2026). Numeric dates with slashes are flagged as ambiguous.
- palette-only: Every colour comes from the house palette or a brand colour role (within a small tolerance). Neutrals (greys, black, white) are allowed unless allowNeutrals is false.
- min-contrast: Text has at least the WCAG contrast ratio against what it sits on (default 4.5, or 3 for large text: 24 px, or 18.66 px bold).
- distinguishable: Series and category colours are far enough apart to tell apart.
- fonts-allowed: Every font is one the house style names: the check's fonts option, else the profile's fonts list, else the brand's heading, body and mono fonts. Generic families (sans-serif, system-ui, ...) are allowed.

Example:
{
  "headingCase": "sentence",
  "maxHeadingLevel": 3,
  "properNouns": [
    "Acme",
    "GitHub"
  ],
  "listItemEnd": "none",
  "quotes": "curly",
  "terms": [
    {
      "avoid": "utilize",
      "use": "use"
    },
    {
      "avoid": "click here",
      "note": "link text says where it goes"
    }
  ],
  "thousandsSeparator": ",",
  "dateFormat": "day-month-year",
  "checks": [
    "heading-case",
    "heading-levels",
    "list-punctuation",
    "quotes",
    "terms",
    "number-format",
    "date-format",
    "fonts-allowed"
  ]
}

<style_domain id="brand" file="brand.json">
Brand: The brand every editor shares: colours by role (primary, text, background, Office slots such as accent1 and dk1), an ordered palette, fonts and a logo, and shared checks to run wherever a domain can be checked against it. Each domain derives its own starting style from it; a domain profile refines that.

Where it goes: brand.json in the skill folder, or under a "brand:" key in the SKILL.md frontmatter (not both). Every domain a skill covers reads its brand.
A variant can build on another skill with "extends: <skill>" in its frontmatter and give only the fields that differ; objects merge field by field, lists and values replace.

Checks it can turn on in "checks" (an id, or { "id": ..., options }):
- palette-only: Every colour comes from the house palette or a brand colour role (within a small tolerance). Neutrals (greys, black, white) are allowed unless allowNeutrals is false.
- min-contrast: Text has at least the WCAG contrast ratio against what it sits on (default 4.5, or 3 for large text: 24 px, or 18.66 px bold).
- distinguishable: Series and category colours are far enough apart to tell apart.
- fonts-allowed: Every font is one the house style names: the check's fonts option, else the profile's fonts list, else the brand's heading, body and mono fonts. Generic families (sans-serif, system-ui, ...) are allowed.

Example:
{
  "name": "Acme",

    "primary": "#0b5fff",
    "secondary": "#ff6a00",
    "accent": "#12a150",
    "text": "#1a1a1a",
    "mutedText": "#5c5c5c",
    "background": "#ffffff",
    "border": "#d9d9d9"
  },
  "fonts": {
    "heading": "Inter",
    "body": "Inter"
  },
  "checks": [
    "palette-only",
    "min-contrast",
    "fonts-allowed"
  ]
}
